cases.detail: legacy_v0+current_v1: Go verify --deep PASS; replay = /hello.txt mode=0644 size=12 sha256=aec5a165bed9d7d50887dc896e73e3e474a636cc071ae3ac03281ee51cf5feae; Go decode+re-encode is byte-identical to the Rust frames
legacy_v0+current_v1: Rust verify --deep PASS on the Go-generated fixtures
Rust wrote rename+hardlink+symlink+sparse(1MiB hole)+xattr+dir tree+overwrite; Go verify --deep PASS, mount read-back identical to Rust's, decode/re-encode byte-identical (108 records)
Go wrote mkdir+create+write+symlink+rename(new)+truncate+sparse+xattr (no Rust-unknown types); Rust verify --deep PASS, mount read-back identical to Go's
Rust rejected the Go volume: orfs: incompatible on-disk format: unknown mandatory record type 0x0017
three handoffs (Go write -> Rust verify+read -> Rust mutate -> Go verify+read -> Go mutate -> Rust verify+read); every handoff verified and read back identically
torn tail at the committed root: Rust verify --deep PASS at root R=10198, committed prefix byte-identical before/after; Go verify+recover PASS and content preserved
SIGKILL of the Rust daemon mid-append: Go verify --deep recovered to a committed boundary and the pre-crash committed file survived
torn frame inside the committed segment: Rust verify --deep PASS at root R=10198 and a read-only mount read-back matches; Go verify --deep PASS; committed prefix byte-identical

Go decode+re-encode is byte-identical to the Rust frames on both Rust fixtures; Go and Rust each read the other's fixtures; Go-vs-Rust builder bytes differ only in identity parameters ( legacy_v0=differs current_v1=differs)

findings.detail: Go emits mandatory record type 0x0017 (CTIME_UPDATE) for hard link / rename-overwrite / chmod / unlink; the Rust reference's registry ends at 0x0015 and refuses an unknown mandatory type, so the Rust reader (verify and mount) rejects the volume

findings.record: writable open on an in-place torn tail
findings.detail: After a torn frame inside the committed segment, a writable open (Go recover/mount, or Rust mount) creates a new segment at the committed root but leaves the stale torn bytes in the committed segment; BOTH readers then fail with 'torn record in non-final segment 0'. Go and Rust behave identically, so this is a shared recovery defect, not a Rust<->Go divergence. A read-only open recovers correctly (the assertions above).

Go-generated and Rust-generated legacy_v0 segments differ (/src/tests/fixtures/legacy_v0/or.log/0000000000000000.seg /rust-fixtures/legacy_v0/or.log/0000000000000000.seg differ: char 62, line 1). Both are valid and mutually readable, but the builders use different volume UUID, segment size, inode timestamps, TX_BEGIN advisory expected_* fields, and record-header inode stamps; the Go codec is nevertheless byte-exact (roundtrip) on the Rust bytes.

Go-generated and Rust-generated current_v1 segments differ (/src/tests/fixtures/current_v1/or.log/0000000000000000.seg /rust-fixtures/current_v1/or.log/0000000000000000.seg differ: char 62, line 1). Both are valid and mutually readable, but the builders use different volume UUID, segment size, inode timestamps, TX_BEGIN advisory expected_* fields, and record-header inode stamps; the Go codec is nevertheless byte-exact (roundtrip) on the Rust bytes.
